definitions: A rule in animal psychology stating that in no case may we interpret an action as the outcome of the exercise of a higher psychical faculty, if it can be interpreted as the outcome of the exercise of one which stands lower in the psychological scale.
The principle that animal behavior should be explained in the simplest possible terms, avoiding complex mental processes if simpler ones suffice.
examples: Morgan's Canon is a foundational principle in comparative psychology.
Researchers often apply Morgan's Canon when studying animal cognition.
Understanding Morgan's Canon helps to avoid anthropomorphism in animal studies.
